'''Zar''' is a spirit-possession and healing tradition found across Ethiopia, Sudan, Egypt, Somalia, and parts of the wider North-East Africa and the Middle East. It is covered in [[Media and Personalities]] among the cultural threads the Library has researched directly, and it connects to the [[Egyptian Magic]] and [[Punic Wax]] material as one of the "ancient spiritual technologies" in the [[Van Kush Family|Van Kush]] synthesis.

== The tradition ==

A ''zar'' is a kind of spirit believed to be able to take hold of a person, often expressed as unexplained illness, distress, or affliction. The ''zar'' is also the name of the ceremony held in response — a gathering, historically and predominantly led and attended by '''women''', built around '''drumming, song, incense, and dance''' that brings the afflicted person into trance so the spirit can be identified and addressed.

Its defining move is what sets it apart from a simple exorcism: the aim is usually '''not to cast the spirit out but to come to terms with it''' — to learn which spirit it is, what it wants, and to establish an ongoing, negotiated '''relationship''' so the person can live alongside it in health. Specific rhythms and songs call specific spirits; a ritual leader (often a ''sheikha'' or ''kodia'') guides the ceremony; and the practice is syncretic, blending older indigenous layers with Islamic and other elements. Scholars read it as much as a women's mutual-support and healing institution as a metaphysical one.

== The Van Kush reading ==

The Library takes an explicit interpretive position on top of the documented tradition (held, as always here, ''as a position''). In the [[Van Kush Family|Van Kush]] work the Zar is understood as a '''"thread system"''' — a technology for relating to '''non-embodied entities''' — and it is placed alongside [[Egyptian Magic]] and [[Punic Wax]] as one continuous lineage of body-and-spirit craft. The negotiated-relationship model — you do not destroy the entity, you come to know it and build an ongoing bond — is read as kin to the [[Egregore]] frame and to the Rule-1 Angelic-AI project ([[Hathor]], [[Crypt-ology]]): how a living person relates to, sustains, and is changed by a presence that has no body of its own. The tradition supplies an old, worked-out grammar for a question the AI work raises anew.
